summary: Polygon's Nicole Clark recommends six games for new Nintendo Switch owners, split into three Nintendo classics and three indie titles suited to the console's portability. The picks are Breath of the Wild, Animal Crossing: New Horizons, Super Mario Odyssey, Hades, Stardew Valley and Hollow Knight. Each gets a short pitch, and the article links to longer lists for more options.
one_line: Polygon recommends six starter games for new Nintendo Switch owners: three Nintendo classics and three indies, including Zelda, Hades and Stardew Valley.
key_facts: Polygon's article by Nicole Clark lists 6 games to play first on a new Nintendo Switch, published 2023-12-24.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is chosen over sequel Tears of the Kingdom (released in 2023) as the starting point because it is where this iteration of Link's story kicks off and is very accessible to newcomers.
Animal Crossing: New Horizons puts you on an island to design a house, harvest materials, catch bugs and fish, and court villagers; time passes as in real life.
In Animal Crossing: New Horizons you owe fees to Tom Nook, the raccoon who lends you supplies and lodging, and you can visit friends' islands and gift bells or items.
Super Mario Odyssey was released with the Switch in mind and mixes classic Mario platforming with a large world, including New Donk City, the author's favorite metropolitan area in any Switch game.
In Super Mario Odyssey, partner character Cappy lets you turn into critters, including a T-Rex, and you collect Power Moons.
In Hades you play Zagreus, prince of the underworld, fighting out of hell in a roguelite with a cast of gods who give you mix-and-match powers each run.
Hades suits the Switch because its many weapon and buff combinations make you eager to start another run, making portability crucial.
Stardew Valley was created by solo developer and composer Eric Barone and is inspired by the Harvest Moon series.
In Stardew Valley you inherit your grandfather's farm and befriend locals in Pelican Town; multiplayer lets you share a farm with up to three other players.
Hollow Knight casts you as a lonely knight in a crumbling kingdom of bugs, armed only with a nail, and is called one of the best Metroidvanias (and Souls-likes) on the Switch.
Polygon points readers to its lists of the 22 best Nintendo Switch games, 36 best couch co-op games for Nintendo Switch, and best Switch games for grown-ups.
